semantic_anchor: A catalogue name identifies a record; sensor readings describe the object and make comparison possible.
prompt: Rich, cinematic yet clean educational space illustration on a deep navy starfield with a faint distant galaxy. Three celestial bodies in a single row from left to right: LEFT: planet Earth with blue oceans, green-brown continents and white clouds, medium size. MIDDLE: an alien ocean world slightly smaller than Earth: mostly deep teal ocean with many small scattered green-and-ochre island chains, a white polar cap and swirling white clouds. No large continents at all, so it cannot be mistaken for Earth. RIGHT: a banded tan-and-orange gas giant whose diameter is TWICE the diameter of Earth in the image, the dominant body in the scene, still fully visible inside the frame. Earth and the middle planet are smaller to leave room for it. Above each body, one small robotic space probe with solar panels shines a thin cyan scanning beam down onto that body. Directly below each body is a small dark glass name plate, then an identical dark holographic readout panel. Name plates, exactly: left 'Earth', middle 'Object-417', right 'Object-892'. Each readout panel is a simple two-column text table with exactly three rows in the same order: a label column and a value column. No bars, no gauges, no charts, no icons inside the panels: only text. Earth panel rows exactly: 'Size  6,371 km', 'Temp  15 °C', 'Air  N2 + O2'. Object-417 panel rows exactly: 'Size  5,900 km', 'Temp  22 °C', 'Air  N2 + O2'. Object-892 panel rows exactly: 'Size  70,000 km', 'Temp  -150 °C', 'Air  H2 + He'. Title across the top in clean white sans-serif: 'Names identify. Sensor readings describe.' Small subtitle under the title: 'Same three readings for every object'. Text must be sharp, horizontal, correctly spelled and fully legible; generous margins; nothing cropped.
acceptance_criteria: Exactly three bodies and three probes; exactly three name plates with the exact names; exactly three readout panels, each with exactly the three rows Size, Temp, Air in that order with the exact values given; the exact title and subtitle; all text legible and correctly spelled.
prohibited_content: Any other words, numbers or labels; word tokens such as cat or the; question marks; cubes; neural network diagrams; arrows; legends; backpropagation; error signals; extra planets with labels; misspellings; watermarks; cropped text. Gauge bars, progress bars, charts or icons inside the readout panels; recognizable Earth continents on the middle planet.
alt_text: Space probes scan Earth, Object-417 and Object-892. Each object has a name plate and the same three readings: size, temperature and air.

semantic_anchor: Why not leave the rows random?
prompt: Cream background, legible navy text and teal/orange cards. Show the matched illustrative contexts cat sat ___ the mat and dog sat ___ the mat, both checked against on. Cat and dog are input clues with separate IDs and rows. These are not quoted corpus examples or measured neighbours.
acceptance_criteria: Two distinct input contexts, one common checking answer on; cat and dog remain distinct. Locally rendered by sentence_illustrations in generate_sensor_analogy_diagrams.py.
prohibited_content: Invented neural values, synonyms claimed identical, merged IDs, geometry improvement claimed without measurements.
alt_text: Cat and dog can supply useful clues for the same on answer while retaining separate word profiles.

semantic_anchor: Where do we get practice questions?
prompt: Cream educational diagram. Title The text already supplies the answer. State running sentence the cat sat on the mat. Show its last complete five-word window cat sat on the mat, then cat sat ___ the mat. Keep on separate as the checking answer. No mask token is supplied to the model.
acceptance_criteria: Five positions in each window; only on becomes a gap; four visible clues; separate on answer. State that six words supply two five-word windows with centers sat and on. Locally rendered by sentence_illustrations in generate_sensor_analogy_diagrams.py.
prohibited_content: Sleepy, extra tokens, BERT mask input, current answer supplied as its own clue, fabricated probabilities.
alt_text: The last five-word window hides on, retaining cat, sat, the and mat as CBOW clues.

semantic_anchor: How does checking a guess teach rows?
prompt: Cream educational diagram. Fetch and average cat, sat, the and mat rows, then a separate predictor makes vocabulary scores. Check against on. Feedback branches to fetched input rows and predictor weights. IDs stay fixed. on's input row is unread in this isolated question; its separate output weights can learn.
acceptance_criteria: Correct clue/answer separation, two parameter-update routes, no neural values. Locally rendered by sentence_illustrations in generate_sensor_analogy_diagrams.py.
prohibited_content: Updating IDs, claiming every input row changes in an isolated lookup step, tying input and output weights, invented loss.
alt_text: Checking on teaches both the predictor and the fetched cat, sat, the and mat profiles; integer IDs stay fixed.

semantic_anchor: Encoder-decoder: ordered log, compact briefing, likely report
prompt: Cream diagram with an observing log, one compact encoder briefing and a decoder report. Actual source the -> cat -> sat. Actual checking answers on -> the -> mat -> eos. Only final encoder state is handed to writer. Prediction concerns vocabulary tokens, not physical measurements.
acceptance_criteria: Three ordered source words, four checking answers including EOS; training reference is not claimed generated output. Locally rendered by observatory in generate_sensor_analogy_diagrams.py.
prohibited_content: Sleepy, fabricated observations, invented model success, attention already implemented, writer access to every source state.
alt_text: An ordered log becomes a briefing and a likely report; the actual source the cat sat is checked against on the mat eos.
